newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk says fire halts two furnaces.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk says fire halts two furnaces.

text.p: A weekend fire at a nickel smelting plant which is part of the flagship combine of Russia's Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS metals group forced two out of five furnaces to shut down, a Norilsk spokesman said on Tuesday.

Anatoly Komrakov said little output had been lost as a result of the fire because the furnaces were already working below capacity. He could not say how long it would take to restore the furnaces to working order.

"There was spillage of molten ore from one of the furnaces which had just been repaired. This got into the cooling system which then caught fire," Komrakov said. "As a result of that fire, two furnaces out of five at the plant stopped producing. Two workers received serious burns in the accident."

He said the fire took place at the Nickel Factory on July 18 at night and that as of July 20 there had been little impact on output. He also said the company's goal of boosting metals output sharply this year was still achievable.

The Nickel Factory is one of three nickel smelting plants in the Norilsk group. Two of the plants, the Nickel Factory and the Nadezhdinsky Factory, are part of the group's main metals combine in the Arctic town of Norilsk. The Norilsk group's third nickel smelter is the Pechenga plant on the Kola Peninsula.

A western analyst said that in 1996, the Nickel Factory produced 60,000 tonnes of nickel, the Nadezhdinsky Factory 76,000 tonnes and the Pechenga Factory 42,000 tonnes, taking the Norilsk group's total nickel output last year to around 178,000 tonnes.
